Corintar (B02)

Survey-region classification: Escann.

In brief: Starting with the adventuring company left after Corin's death, let the half-orc Lothane turn his companions' oath into a new order in Escann—and confront the shadow within their crusading ideal.

Story: Very high | Mission-tree length: Long (53 direct B02 missions) | Mission-tree update: Based on the local scripts supporting EU4 v1.37.5.0 | Distinctiveness: Very high | Tedium: Moderately high (religious phases and prolonged reconstruction) | Early pressure: High | Expansion: High, with the later goal of unifying Escann

Those Corin Left Behind

The scoring table spells the name “Corintar” in Chinese as 科林塔尔; the current local Chinese localisation's official name for B02 is 科琳塔尔. In 1444 it is already an adventuring-company polity in Escann: its country history sets the Regent Court faith, a theocracy, and an Adventurer reform. Its starting leader is the half-orc Lothane “Bluetusk” Sirmuna. It is not a later formable, and the later state religion of Corinite theocracy and its purges must not be projected back onto the opening government.【Local localisation】【Local history script】

Corin herself had already become a legend after the war against the Dookanson and the Greentide, but her companions had to deal with mundane problems: farmland ruined by the Greentide, displaced residents, a knightly order without stable finances, and a border where orcs and humans still fought. Mission flavour starts from Bluetusk's memories, bringing the friends, disputes, and sacrifices behind Corin's sword back down to earth. Returning to the fields, rebuilding towns, and training recruits are not decoration for a grand religious war; they are the foundation that gives an adventuring company the standing to discuss a country's future.【Local flavour text】【Local script】

The offline Wiki's entries on the people and companions confirm the organisation's succession: after Corin's death, Bluetusk and the surviving companions formed Corintar and continued their pursuit of peace and fight against what they considered evil. This source explains why the adventuring company exists; it does not provide a detailed history of each territory B02 later acquires. That must be grounded in local starting history and missions. Because the organisation was born at the moment it lost its leader, Bluetusk's memories in the missions are not prophecy but a living person's interpretation of a friend's ideals.【Wiki】

From Monastery to Crusade

Early missions rebuild Escann while establishing Corintar chapters in the Empire, Gawed, and elsewhere, recruiting the faithful and military officers. Monasteries provide education and training as farmsteads, cities, and churches are rebuilt. This network supplies manpower and influence for later religious politics, but also gives each chapter its own interests. The player must manage diplomatic relations, religious requirements, and a transnational organisation—not simply select the next conquest target—to advance Corin's cause.【Local script】【Local flavour text】

The story hardens after the rise of Corinite faith. Flavour text for the “Edict of Corin's Fall” requires administrators to swear violence against those deemed faithless; the Crusaders' purges and the “Great Purge” then tie political leadership to absolute devotion. The current script makes the Great Purge a mission in the later religious chain and triggers events involving the chapters. It is not war or conversion to Corinite faith by itself that makes the country evil: the state explicitly adopts religious scrutiny and coercion as instruments of government. The specific harm to civilians caused by the purges still requires checking event branches; the mission title alone does not establish a massacre.【Local flavour text】【Local script】

Reconciliation, Orcs, and Escann

The mission tree does not stop at fanaticism. Flavour text says that chapters which left after the Great Purge continue supporting Corin's cause in secret; the later “Reconciliation” tries to bring them back into the New Corintar. The missions also make a clearer public commitment regarding orcs: negotiate with neighbouring clans, help Red-Teeth orc communities put down roots, and demand an end to orcish enslavement. Bluetusk's attitude toward former enemies is not pure revenge either; he wants clans that once persecuted him to have the chance to accept Corin's light. These details provide concrete evidence of pluralist practice, rather than earning credit through an equality slogan alone.【Local flavour text】【Local script】

The late game still asks the country to pay for Escann's walls, passes, farmland, and industry. Mission text even makes the country look back at destruction caused by its own wars and ask whether those harms accord with Corin's will. The endgame ideal is to free Escann from the Greentide and civil war and carry Corin's cause beyond the country's borders. But “lasting peace after unification” is a future the mission narrative hopes to realise, not settled history in 1444 and not proof that every player route is cost-free.【Local flavour text】

This self-examination is the strongest narrative turn. Corintar can sincerely protect farmers and include orcs while allowing excessively devout officials to harm dissenters; the article should not define it only by the first half. The need to seek out departed comrades after the purge shows that “who has the right to represent Corin?” matters more than a simple change of country name. This is not a pure victory story, but an organisation repeatedly testing its creed through state-building, failure, and attempted correction.【Local flavour text】

Personality and Recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 82/100 | Autocracy 69/100 | Magic–Artifice 75/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 67/100) | Pluralism 78/100. The phase profile shifts from adventuring-company reconstruction (Expansion 60, Autocracy 55) to the Corinite purge (Autocracy 85, Pluralism 42), then to reconciliation in the New Corintar (Pluralism 78).

The v2.1 values rating is Good (71/100), with a mixed trajectory. The phase scores are: return and postwar reconstruction (Good, 74/100) → the Great Purge and religious scrutiny (Neutral, 49/100) → chapter reconciliation and opposition to orcish enslavement (Good, 78/100). Return and reconstruction, monastic education, orc equality, and ending enslavement have clear positive evidence; the administrative oath, chapter purges, and coercive religious scrutiny seriously weaken restraint. The details of purge casualties have not been checked event by event. War and religious propagation alone do not count against the score.

Across these phases, the country's values do not rise in a straight line from the Greentide war toward the good: it may fall into zealotry in the middle and seek reconciliation later, so each phase must be assessed separately. Returning people, public reconstruction, opposition to enslavement, and orc equality count positively; the administrative oath, chapter purges, and coercive proselytising reduce restraint. The phase scores are Good 74/100 → Neutral 49/100 → Good 78/100.

Recommended for players seeking a self-critical religious epic, an adventuring company becoming a state, and the rebuilding of Escann. Avoid it if you dislike waiting through religious phases and complex chapter prerequisites, or only want to play an unambiguous holy knight.

Player discussions often recommend Corintar to newcomers to Escann, while warning that the rise of Corinite faith, neighbouring expansion, and the timing of religious wars can slow the mission chain. These are version-specific impressions, not a guarantee of current event timing.【Community view】

See the Chinese-source evidence page for the exact boundaries of the offline Wiki, related official diaries, and player posts.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces current national traditions, seven national ideas and ambition. Traditions apply on adoption, ideas unlock through investment, and ambition follows completion of all seven. Only national ideas are listed, not racial, governmental or mission bonuses; predecessor and successor sets do not stack. Idea descriptions can recall history or describe future ideals and do not automatically establish events before 1444.

Effect displays and units are inherited for source parity, not independently certified; uncertain percentages remain accompanied by script keys and raw values.

Corintar (B02) — Corintari Ideas

Set ID: B02_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Corintari Traditions

  • May recruit female generals: Allowed (may_recruit_female_generals; raw value yes).

  • Leaders without upkeep: +1 (free_leader_pool; raw value 1).

  • Discipline: +5% (discipline; raw value 0.05).

1. She Protects, but also Attacks

The old god of war Agrados was known for his ferocious rage and unyielding blows against his enemies, but Corin saw differently. She saw equal merit in using her powers not only to strike at her foes, but to use them to protect her faithful just the same - no such event can be compared to the Battle of Castonath when Corin raised her shield to defend Lothane Bluetusk from a killing blow by Korgus Dookanson himself, knowing that it would leave her exposed to Korgus' off-hand attack. Accepting her purpose, she used this moment of defense to return the favour and slew Korgus at the cost of her life, ending the Greentide once and for all.

  • Army morale: +10% (land_morale; raw value 0.1).

2. Bluetusk Reforms

Lothane Bluetusk was a loyal friend and companion of Corin and the first Grandmaster of the Corintar. While Corin's ideals started the Corintar, it was Lothane's work that organized the order into a legitimate force.

  • Development cost: -10% (development_cost; raw value -0.1).

3. Heroes of the Greentide

Corin. Lothane Bluetusk. Dominic of Gallowspeak. Eledas Silurion. All of these names and a dozen more of Corin's Circle have become household names across all of Cannor. We as their successors have big shoes to fill, but their heroism and legacy will never leave us.

  • Prestige decay: -1% (prestige_decay; raw value -0.01).

4. One People, One Religion

Unlike others, we can claim no exalted lineage nor storied ancestry. We are merely honest men and women from a dozen races and cultures who came together because we believed in something and someone- Corin. Let us promote a new order based on ideals, not origins!

  • True faith tolerance: +1 (tolerance_own; raw value 1).

  • Yearly corruption: -0.05 (yearly_corruption; raw value -0.05).

5. To Purge Evil

"For goodness without action means nothing,

And from nothing, the roots of evil will fester,

For our shields protect, and our swords strike true,

And evil purged means a world saved."

-Corinite Creed

  • War exhaustion: -0.02 (war_exhaustion; raw value -0.02).

  • Missionary strength: +1% (global_missionary_strength; raw value 0.01).

6. Rise of the Corinite Crusaders

As more and more people were converted to the Corinite faith, more and more people felt the zeal that her will must be spread across all. This ever-growing group were known as the Corinite Crusaders, and warred across Cannor and even Anbennar itself hoping to bring justice to world.

  • Manpower recovery speed: +10% (manpower_recovery_speed; raw value 0.1).

  • Army maintenance modifier: -5% (land_maintenance_modifier; raw value -0.05).

7. Agents of New Corintar

When the old Corintar was disbanded and the affairs of the state were under control of the Corinite Crusaders, a new splinter group consisting of moderate Corinites formed a semi-secret society called the New Corintar. These members worked all across the world to secretly ensure that Corin's ideals of freedom, justice and good of man were upheld even beyond the borders of the Corintari state.

  • Diplomatic reputation: +100% (diplomatic_reputation; raw value 1).

  • Spy network construction: +20% (spy_offence; raw value 0.2).
